confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your site and logo say “Yokes Master Plumbing,” your Google listing says “Yoke's master plumbing and remodeling,” and your email is yokesplumbingnremodeling@gmail.com, so which spelling and name should every listing use?
Your site shows no street address, while your Google listing puts you at 718 N Milstead St, so which address should every listing use?
Your site names no one, while your Google reviews name Dan, Tammy, Jake and Brandon, so who should the site introduce, and in what role?
Your reviews describe leaks that others couldn't find, and the site says you go after the source, so how does your team find a hidden leak, and what should we say about it?

lead.heading: Why we led with finding the leak
lead.text: The scariest moment for a Wichita homeowner is water coming from somewhere nobody can find. We led with that because it is built on things Google can't find anywhere else: a customer's real account of a gas leak the gas company couldn't locate, the way your reviews describe your work, and Wichita details like the warm floor and the doubled water bill. That is also what helps you rank.
